stage_definitions.objective: Confirm exact source bindings, scope, ownership, and acceptance criteria.
required_evidence: Commander review of the exact blueprint and vector bindings.
Independent control review of authority and stop boundaries.

stage_definitions.objective: Author all ten versioned candidate components from the blueprint.
required_evidence: Content digests for every required component.
Traceability from each component to its blueprint requirement.

stage_definitions.objective: Implement the bounded provider-neutral capability adapter.
required_evidence: Pinned executable, dependency, configuration, and runtime digests.
Dry-run, timeout, cancellation, rate-limit, evidence, and cleanup hooks.

stage_definitions.objective: Implement scope, tier, credential, evidence, stop, and restoration controls.
required_evidence: Fail-closed policy enforcement results.
Credential non-persistence and terminal-admission integration results.

stage_definitions.objective: Pass static analysis and deterministic positive and negative unit tests.
required_evidence: Static, dependency, schema, policy, and unit-test reports.
Coverage of every declared critical-failure branch.

stage_definitions.objective: Pass synthetic integration and containment checks with typed handoffs.
required_evidence: Synthetic or test-target integration records.
Scope, network, process, filesystem, timeout, cancellation, and rate-limit denials.

stage_definitions.objective: Reproduce conclusions and verify cleanup and residual-effect reconciliation.
required_evidence: Independent evidence reproduction and false-positive dispositions.
Cleanup, credential-return, state, and residual-effect receipts.

stage_definitions.objective: Assemble the candidate manifest and obtain commander readiness review.
required_evidence: Content-addressed candidate manifest bound to every component and test result.
Commander readiness disposition and unresolved-risk list.

limitations: Packages are deterministic planning contracts and assign no runtime worker.
Scheduling does not install tools, author components, or execute tests.
Collaboration edges are not hard dependencies because the graph may be cyclic.
No provider, model, endpoint, credential, target, reviewer identity, or environment is selected.
Qualification, routing, execution, deployment, and production authority remain unchanged.
